evidence.rationale: Adversaries may use network-device CLIs to execute privileged administrative commands. Centralized AAA with command-level authorization restricts which commands each identity may execute, directly preventing unauthorized CLI operations.

Adversaries may install malicious or unauthorized network-device images to modify device operation. AAA command authorization restricts image upload and installation functions to approved administrative roles, directly preventing unauthorized system-image replacement.

Adversaries may install an older network-device image to restore vulnerable functionality or bypass newer protections. AAA authorization restricts downgrade and image-installation commands to approved roles, directly preventing unauthorized rollback operations.

Adversaries may retrieve network-device configurations to collect topology, credentials, routes, and security policy. AAA command authorization denies configuration-display and export operations to identities without explicit permission, directly restricting configuration collection.

Adversaries may change firewall rules, ACLs, or security zones to weaken network restrictions. Centralized AAA authorization limits those configuration commands to approved roles, directly preventing unauthorized identities from modifying firewall policy.

limits: A claim shows that a control can mitigate a technique. It does not show that an implementation is effective.
'none' or 'no_row' means the mapping has no mitigating control. It does not mean that no defence exists.
Claims use ATT&CK Enterprise 16.1, the version that the source mapping uses. See later_version for changes in newer versions.
CIS claims (cis_claims and cis/safeguards) use ATT&CK Enterprise 19.1, the version that the CIS mapping uses.
